_readme: What each recorded hold clip SAYS, and whether it ends open.
The clip is audio, so nothing downstream can read its words. Two things
need them: join_after_head, to make the model's reply continue the clause
rather than restart after it, and the duplicate-opener strip, so the model
does not say the same sentence 1-2s later.
open_clause is the important field. A CLOSED clip ends in a full stop or
the ellipsis -- ElevenLabs renders that as a falling contour plus a pause,
which is the canned-filler sound -- and it must be the ONLY hold speech in
its turn, or the caller hears two ways of saying the same thing. An OPEN
clip is an unfinished clause the situational head continues:
[clip 350ms] 'Let me just check -'
[head  600ms] '... what Saturday looks like -'
[reply]       'half past nine in the morning is free.'
So open_clause=false means the clip latches _hold_head_spoken and nothing
else speaks; open_clause=true means it records its wording for the join but
leaves the latch clear so the head may follow.
THE SHIPPED CLIP IS CLOSED. Changing this flag without recutting the audio
makes the caller hear 'Let me just check that for you...' followed by 'Let
me see what Saturday looks like -', which is the exact double-phrase defect
the arbiter exists to remove. Recut first, then flip it.
Recutting needs the LIVE ElevenLabs voice. It is a paid Voice Library
voice: a free key returns 402 and synthesise_filler falls back to a
different voice, which is how a clip in the wrong person's voice shipped
once already. Run scripts/synthesise_filler.py with the live key.

filler_checking.text: Let me just check that for you…
